facts.claim: Include JSDoc comments describing functions.
Use semantic HTML elements (e.g. blockquote, figure) when building block DOM.
Use the spread operator to append multiple elements at once: container.append(...nodes).
Use element.replaceChildren() to replace a block's content efficiently.
Query within the block (block.querySelectorAll) rather than the whole document.
Avoid innerHTML for complex structures (maintainability, XSS risk); build with DOM APIs.
Don't mutate elements belonging to other blocks or global page regions (e.g. header) from a block.
Don't leave obsolete/temporary DOM elements; replace originals (e.g. p.replaceWith(newDiv)).
Check for variant classes with classList.contains().
Use async/await with try/catch for data fetching and log failures.
Use static imports for always-needed modules and dynamic import() for conditional or deferrable modules.
Defer expensive work (e.g. setTimeout) and keep initial decoration minimal.
Use IntersectionObserver to load heavy content (e.g. embeds) only when the block becomes visible.
Use ES6+ features (const/let, arrow functions, template literals).
Naming: camelCase for variables/functions, PascalCase for classes, UPPER_CASE for constants.
Write CSS mobile-first: defaults for small screens, media queries for larger.
Use CSS custom properties instead of hardcoded colors/fonts when variables exist.
Use logical properties (padding-inline, margin-inline-start, etc.) for internationalization.
Prefer flexbox/grid with gap for layout; grid repeat(auto-fit, minmax()) for responsive grids.
Use BEM-like descriptive class names for elements within a block.
Avoid generic class names like .container or .wrapper; be block-specific.
Keep specificity low: use classes over tags, avoid IDs, keep selector chains short (2-3 levels).
Variant styles use compound selectors on the block (.my-block.dark), and can be combined (.my-block.dark.wide).
Prefer transforms over position changes (left/top) to avoid reflow.
Use will-change sparingly, only for elements that will animate.
Be careful with expensive properties (box-shadow, border-radius, opacity, filters) on large areas.
CSS formatting: one selector per line, brace on selector line, one property per line, space after colon, none before, semicolon after every declaration.
Recommended property order: layout, box model, visual, animation/transform.
Common patterns: list reset, centering with max-width + margin-inline:auto, aspect-ratio, text truncation with ellipsis.
Don't use !important; fix specificity instead.
Don't use absolute positioning for layout; reserve it for visual effects.
Make core (shared) changes before dependent block changes, test them independently, and keep them minimal since they affect many pages.
Document core changes with code comments rather than separate docs.
